s1.syndrome_frame: A cardiac abnormality with a systolic murmur and abnormal ECG findings in a young pregnant woman
salient_findings: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Complete right bundle-branch block with fragmented QRS on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle with a large defect and left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
key_facts: 29-year-old primigravida woman
No history of dyspnea, chest pain, palpitation, or lower limb swelling
Vital parameters within normal limits
Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region
Normal sinus rhythm with heart rate of 70 beats/min on ECG
Complete right bundle-branch block with normal PR interval on ECG
Fragmented QRS with a notch on the R wave in inferior leads on ECG
Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography
Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography
Normal cardiac output on right-sided heart catheterization
Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium
Pulmonary vascular resistance: 1.8 Wood units

shortlist.label: Ostium Secundum Atrial Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Dilated right atrium and right ventricle on echocardiography

shortlist.label: Atrial Septal Defect
shortlist.why_kept: Systolic murmur in the left upper parasternal region and abnormal ECG findings

shortlist.label: Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection
shortlist.why_kept: Step-up in oxygenation from superior vena cava to right atrium

shortlist.label: Scimitar Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Anomalous pulmonary venous connection suggested by echocardiography and oxygenation step-up

raw.rationale: The presence of a large 21-mm defect with left-to-right shunt, dilated right atrium and right ventricle, and a step-up in oxygenation from the superior vena cava to the right atrium are consistent with an ostium secundum atrial septal defect.

rejected.label: Sinus Venosus Atrial Septal Defect
rejected.why: Typically associated with partial anomalous pulmonary venous connection, which is not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Atrial Septal Defect
rejected.why: Too general, as there are multiple types of atrial septal defects

rejected.label: Partial Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connection
rejected.why: Not directly supported by the echocardiography findings, which show a large defect with left-to-right shunt

rejected.label: Scimitar Syndrome
rejected.why: Characterized by anomalous pulmonary venous connection to the inferior vena cava, which is not described in the case
